lessons.name: What is Node.js? — JavaScript outside the browser
lessons.desc: Node.js is a runtime that lets you run JavaScript on a server (not just in a browser). Built on Chrome's V8 engine. Before Node.js (2009), JS could only run in browsers. Now you can build web servers, APIs, CLIs, and scripts with JS.
lessons.q: What is Node.js and why does it matter that JavaScript can run outside the browser?
lessons.qsub: Node.js is why the same language (JS) works on both frontend and backend. It's the foundation of the entire npm ecosystem.
terms: JS ko browser ke bahar chalane wala environment — Node.js ek runtime hai.
Google ka C++ JS engine jo JS ko machine code banata hai.
Node events (callbacks) par chalta hai, har kaam async.
Packages install karne ka registry — JS ki duniya ka app store.
lessons.what:
Node.js ek runtime environment hai jo JavaScript ko browser ke bahar server par chalata hai. 2009 se pehle JS sirf browser mein chal sakti thi. Node ne V8 engine (Chrome ka) le kar uske upar OS APIs (file, network) jod di.

Matlab ab aap web servers, CLI, tools, microservices sab JS mein bana sakte ho. Same language frontend + backend — ek hi giri (skill) se dono. Ye npm ecosystem ki bhi foundation hai.
lessons.analogy: Car ka engine (V8) alag cheez hai, car body + steering + wheels (OS APIs) alag. Node = V8 engine ko ek puri gaadi mein lagane ka kaam — same engine, ab gaddi seedha chal sakti hai jahan SEO (browser) ki zaroorat nahi.
lessons.why: Backend me JS chalaana = ek hi language frontend+backend, bhari non-blocking I/O, aur npm ka bada ecosystem. Isliye startups se lekar FAANG tak backend Node par bana hai. Interview "what is Node" ka yahi seedha answer.

lessons.name: Installing Node.js and running your first script
lessons.desc: Download from nodejs.org. Run JS files with: node filename.js. Check version: node -v. Node also gives you a REPL (interactive shell): just type node in your terminal.
lessons.q: How do you install Node.js and run your first JavaScript script?
lessons.qsub: What commands do you use to run a file, check your version, and open the interactive REPL?
terms: Kisi .js file ko run karne ka command.
Node version check karne ka command.
Interactive shell — bash me bas node likh kar turant JS try karo.
Naya project ka package.json banata hai.
lessons.what:
Install karne ke baad aap 3 cheezein karte ho: node file.js se script chalao, node -v se version dekho, aur node khol kar REPL (interactive terminal) mein turant JS try karo.

npm init se package.json banata hai — apne project ki identity. Bahut saare beginners npm aur node ko confuse karte hain: node = runtime (JS chalao), npm = package manager (libraries install karo).
lessons.analogy: Kitchen: node = stove + gas (khana banao). npm = sabzi mandi (saamagri le aao). Stove ke bina khana nahi banta, mandi ke bina variety nahi. Dono alag kaam, dono zaroori.
lessons.why: Setup hi aadha interview ready hota hai — bina run kare code likhna possible hi nahi. Version control (nvm se node version switch) aur REPL se chhoti cheez test karna interview dene wale ka daily routine hai. Ye basic hai hi, par machhli ka paani maan lo.

lessons.name: Node.js vs Browser JS — what is different?
lessons.desc: Browser JS has: window, document, DOM, alert(), fetch(). Node.js has NONE of these. Instead, Node.js has: fs (file system), http (create servers), os (OS info), path (file paths), process (env vars, args). Both run the same JS syntax (ES6+) but the APIs are totally different.
lessons.q: What are the key differences between running JavaScript in a browser versus Node.js?
lessons.qsub: Developers switching from frontend to backend get confused because the globals are different. Knowing this upfront saves hours of confusion.
terms: Node global — env vars, args, PID.
Node ka global object (browser ka window wala role).
lessons.what:
Dono ek hi JS syntax chalaate hain, par globals alag. Browser: window, document, DOM, alert(), fetch(). Node: inme se koi nahi. Node ke paas: fs (files), http (server), os, path, process (env, args).

Ye confuse frontend developer ko sabse zyada hota hai — window is not defined dekh ke. Understanding upfront = hours ki confusion bacha.
lessons.analogy: Dono Hindi bolte hain (JS syntax) par ek ghar ki rasoie myein (browser: window DOM) aur ek factory mein (Node: fs, http). Wahi shabd, alag watsphoros (utensils).
lessons.why: Isse pata chalta hai Node server-side kyun hai — OS level files/network handle karta. Interview "node vs browser" ka answer: globals + APIs alag, language same. Debugging ke liye bhi zaroori — "window is not defined" ka matlab samajhna.

lessons.name: V8 Engine — what compiles and runs your JavaScript
lessons.desc: V8 is Google's open-source JS engine written in C++. It compiles JS to machine code using JIT (Just-In-Time) compilation. Node.js is literally a C++ program that embeds V8 and adds OS APIs (file system, networking) on top.
lessons.q: What is the V8 engine and how does it make JavaScript fast in Node.js?
lessons.qsub: Understanding V8 explains why JS can be fast, why it has a garbage collector, and why Node.js performance tuning looks at V8 flags.
terms: Google ka C++ JS engine — JS ko machine code banata.
Just-In-Time compilation — runtime par code optimize.
V8 memory manage karta — pehle padh, phir le.
Node ka C layer — event loop + async I/O, V8 ke saath.
lessons.what:
V8 Google ka open-source C++ JS engine hain (Chrome bhi yahi use karta). Ye JS ko JIT se machine code mein compile karta hai — isliye JS fast hai.

Node.js literally ek C++ program hai jo V8 embed karta hai aur upar OS APIs (fs, net) jodta hai. V8 ka GC memory manage karta. Par V8 event loop nahi banata — wo libuv (Node ka C layer) banata hai jo async I/O + thread pool handle karta hai.
lessons.analogy: V8 = ek super-fast translator/engine. Node = us engine ko lagaya hua povra (chassis) jisme OS ke saath baat karne ke parts hain (libuv, fs). V8 sirf JS ka math karta; Node usko duniya (files/network) se jodta.
lessons.why: Isse samajh aa jata hai JS fast kyun (JIT), GC kyun, aur Node perf tuning V8 flags par kyun dekhate. Interview deep dive ka first step — V8 vs Node boundary clear.

lessons.name: npm — managing packages and dependencies
lessons.desc: npm (Node Package Manager) is the world's largest software registry. npm install express downloads the Express package to node_modules/. package.json tracks your dependencies. package-lock.json locks exact versions for reproducible installs.
lessons.q: How does npm work? What is the purpose of package.json and package-lock.json?
lessons.qsub: Almost every Node.js project uses npm packages. Understanding package.json, scripts, and versioning prevents broken deploys.
terms: Node Package Manager — duniya ka sabse bada package registry.
Dependencies, scripts, metadata — project ki identity.
lessons.what:
npm JS packages install karta hai. npm install express Express ko node_modules/ mein download karta hai aur package.json mein add.

package.json: app ki identity (dependencies, scripts). package-lock.json: exact versions lock karta hai taaki har machine par wahi version install ho (reproducible). package.json mein ranges ho sakte (^1.2.3), lock mein exact.
lessons.analogy: Recipe book (package.json) likhta hai "2 cups atta (^ = koi bhi 2-cup wala)". Shopping list locked (package-lock.json) tasveer ke saath "ye exact brand ka atta" — isliye kitchen sab jagah ek jaisi bani.
lessons.why: Reproducible builds production ka base hai. Lock file na hones se "mere machine par chal raha hai" wala classic bug. Scripts (npm run build) CI/CD mein use — iska code rehna must.

lessons.name: Event Loop: phases overview (timers, poll, check, close)
lessons.desc: Node.js event loop is a C/libuv loop that processes 6 phases in order: timers, pending callbacks, idle/prepare, poll, check, close.
lessons.q: Walk me through the phases of the Node.js event loop. What happens in each phase?
lessons.qsub: The event loop is the beating heart of Node.js async I/O — understanding phases prevents callback hell and timing surprises.
terms: libuv ka C loop — 6 phases, callback/async kaal.
lessons.what:
Node ka event loop ek round-robin C loop hai (libuv) jo 6 phases order mein chalaata hai: timers → pending → idle → poll → check → close. Har tick par ek phase ka queue process hota hai.

Timers: setTimeout. Poll: I/O callbacks (file, network) — yahan sabse zyada wait. Check: setImmediate. Close: cleanup. Loop tab tak chalta jab tak koi work poccha hote.
lessons.analogy: Railway station (event loop): har phase ek platform (timers, poll, check). Train (loop) systematic order se har platform par rukti hai aur jo passenger (callback) ready hai use uthati. Koi ready nahi to next round.
lessons.why: Ye Node ke async I/O ka dil hai. Phases na samjho to callback timing, order bugs, performance sab galat. Interview ka sabse deep "event loop walk-through" yahi hai.

lessons.name: Microtasks vs Macrotasks: nextTick, Promise, setImmediate
lessons.desc: Microtasks (nextTick, Promise.then, queueMicrotask) run between each macrotask, creating a priority queue system.
lessons.q: What is the difference between microtasks and macrotasks in Node.js? What is the execution order?
lessons.qsub: Mastering microtask scheduling prevents subtle ordering bugs and is a classic interview deep-dive.
terms: Current operation khatam hote hi, sabse pehle.
Check phase — agle round khilari wala.
lessons.what:
Microtasks (nextTick, Promise.then) har single operation ke baad chalte hain — isline ye macrotasks se pehle. Macrotasks (setTimeout, I/O, setImmediate) agli phase/round mein.

process.nextTick sabse agla hai — technically ye phase mein nahi, balki har call-slice ke baad apna queue drain karta hai. Promise.then microtask queue se. Order: nextTick > promise > macrotask.
lessons.analogy: ATM queue: macrotask = log (bahut log). Microtask = VIP lane jo har baar turant parey zyada. nextTick = "sabse VIP VIP" — har incomplete transaction ke turant baad iska number pehle aata, phir promise VIP.
lessons.why: Ordering bugs isi se aate hain — "setTimeout(...,0) promise se pehle kyun nahi chala?" — kyunki microtask pehle. Ye subtle ordering classic FAANG deep dive hai.

lessons.name: libuv internals: async I/O, thread pool, epoll/kqueue
lessons.desc: libuv abstracts OS async I/O using epoll (Linux), kqueue (macOS), IOCP (Windows). File system operations use a thread pool.
lessons.q: How does libuv handle async I/O under the hood? What role does the thread pool play?
lessons.qsub: libuv is the C layer that makes Node.js async I/O possible — knowing it separates Node devs from architects.
terms: Node ka C library — async I/O, event loop, thread pool.
Linux ka I/O multiplexing (file changes pe notify).
libuv ke 4 (default) threads — fs, DNS, crypto ye use.
lessons.what:
libuv Node ko async I/O de ta hai. OS-level event notification: Linux par epoll, macOS par kqueue, Windows par IOCP.

Network I/O (net, tcp) in OS mechanisms se non-blocking hota — ek hi thread, kai sockets. Par file system, DNS, crypto OS ko aise non-blocking support nahi hota (file ops blocking), isliye libuv unhe thread pool (default 4 threads) par dada hai. Wahan result callback hota hai.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant manager (main thread) sirf ek hai — waiters ke orders (callbacks) complete hone par hi leta hai (event loop). Par kitchen helpers (thread pool) brigade asmaan — file padhna/cooking jaisa blocking kaam in 4 helpers (threads) mein bant jaata so manager ruk nahi.
lessons.why: Isse pata chalta hai NODE KYA karta hai OS ke saath — network epoll se, file/crypto thread pool se. Ye "na light sume" separation architect-level knowledge hai. Interview "libuv, thread pool, epoll" yahi answer.

lessons.name: Timers: setTimeout, setInterval, setImmediate internals
lessons.desc: Timers are stored in a sorted min-heap inside libuv. setImmediate runs in the check phase of the event loop.
lessons.q: How do setTimeout, setInterval, and setImmediate work internally? When does each one fire?
lessons.qsub: Timers are the most common async primitive — knowing their internal precision and ordering is essential.
terms: Min-heap (timers) par; minimum delay ka scheduled.
Har delay par repeat; recursive timers.
Check phase — current poll ke baad.
Sorted timeout structure — sabse chhota deadline pehle.
lessons.what:
Timers libuv ke andar ek sorted min-heap mein stored hote hain — jiska deadline sabse pehle (chhota) wo sabse pehle. setTimeout(fn, 0) bhi 0ms nahi, minimum ~1ms + phase delay.

setImmediate timers ka naheen — ye check phase mein chalta hai. setTimeout(...,0) vs setImmediate — inside I/O callback, setImmediate hamesha pehle; top-level par order environment-dependent.
lessons.analogy: Alarm clock wall: saare timers ek min-heap board par chipke hain, sabse jaldi ka alarm pehle bajta. setImmediate = "main is station se aage check wale platform par chalunga, routine wait nahi" wala fast-pass.
lessons.why: Timers ki precision aur ordering interview ka favourite. setImmediate vs setTimeout(0) ka subtle ordering — aur timer "0ms" myth — production scheduling bugs bhi yahi. Cheap but important.

lessons.name: async/await and Promise execution order in event loop
lessons.desc: Async/await is syntactic sugar over Promises. Awaited continuations are queued as .then() microtasks after the promise resolves.
lessons.q: How does async/await interact with the event loop? When exactly does the awaited code resume?
lessons.qsub: Promise microtask ordering with the event loop is one of the most common tricky interview questions at FAANG.
terms: Rukta nahi thread — scheduler ko control de deta, phir wapas.
lessons.what:
async/await sirf Promises ke upar sugar hai. await x actually x.then(continuation) banata hai — jo microtask queue mein aata hai callback.

Await block nahi karata — wo function ko "suspend" karta hai, event loop ko kaam deta hai, aur jab promise resolve-hota to microtask mein continuation resume hota hai next tick ke pehle. Order: synchronous code > microtasks > macrotasks.
lessons.analogy: Waiter (event loop) ek customer (async fn) ko order deta (await) — "khana ready jab aaye tab bulana". Waiter rukta nahi, doosre tables par kaam karta. Jab khana ready (promise resolve) → kisi agle pause par (microtask) us customer ke paas apna khana (continuation) laata.
lessons.why: Promise/async ordering is sabse common tricky FAANG question. "Awaited code kab resume hota?" ka answer: microtask, agle phase se pehle. Isse concurrency bugs aur perf samajh aate hain.

lessons.name: EventEmitter patterns: memory leaks, maxListeners
lessons.desc: EventEmitter is Node's pub-sub pattern with on/emit/once. By default warns at 10 listeners per event.
lessons.q: How does the EventEmitter pattern work in Node.js? What causes memory leaks with event listeners?
lessons.qsub: EventEmitter is the foundation of Node.js streams, HTTP, and custom modules — leaks are a common production issue.
terms: Remove nahi kiya listener — object zinda reh jata.
lessons.what:
EventEmitter Node ka pub-sub pattern — on se listener, emit se event fire, once se ek baar waala. Har udne-wala jaisa streams, HTTP, custom modules isi par banned.

Memory leak: jab aap .on() se listener jodte ho aur listener waps hata. removeListener/removeAllListeners nahi, to wo listener + object GC mein nahi jata — unbounded listeners. Default maxListeners=10 par warning.
lessons.analogy: Radio station + subscribers: station (EventEmitter) events broadcast karta (emit); subscribers (listeners) sunte (on). Agar ek subscriber radio band nahi karta (removeListener) to wo channel hamesha baajta rehta — battery (memory) khatam.
lessons.why: Ye pub-sub hi streams/http ka base hai. Production mein leak ka sabse aam cause listener remove na karna. Interview: "EventEmitter leak kaise hota?" — listeners accumulate, event emitter zinda rehta.

lessons.name: AbortController, AbortSignal, and cancellation patterns
lessons.desc: AbortController provides a standard way to cancel async operations via AbortSignal. Node.js adopted the Web API standard.
lessons.q: How does AbortController work in Node.js and what async operations can it cancel?
lessons.qsub: Cancellation is the hardest async pattern — AbortController unifies it across timers, streams, and HTTP.
terms: Async op cancel karne ka standard signal.
lessons.what:
AbortController Node ka standard async-cancel mechanism (Web API se adopt). Aap AbortSignal banao, use timers/streams/HTTP/fetch par pass karo, aur controller.abort() se cancel — wo operations AbortError throw karte.

Pehle har library apna cancel tha (request.abort(), stream.destroy()) — koi ek standard nahi. AbortController unifies. Ye sabse hard async pattern (cancellation) ka modern solution hai.
lessons.analogy: Kitchen order bell: waiter (async op) order le kar jata hai. Aap AbortController bell mein ek "cancel" button (signal) jodte ho. Jab kisi bhi chef (timer/stream/fetch) ko wo signal dikhta aur aap bell bajaate (abort) — chef rukta hai aur "kaam radd (AbortError)" kehta hai.
lessons.why: Cancellation = sabse hard async pattern. User ne badla, request kab gayi — agar cancel na ho to ghost operations resources khaati hain. Node 17.3+ / 18 ab universal AbortController rakhta. Interview "how to cancel async" ka modern answer.

lessons.name: CommonJS: require() resolution algorithm, module.wrapper
lessons.desc: CommonJS modules wrap code in (function(exports, require, module, __filename, __dirname) { ... }). require() resolves, loads, compiles, caches.
lessons.q: How does require() resolve modules in Node.js? What is the module wrapper?
lessons.qsub: The module system is the first thousand lines of code a Node process runs — understanding resolution prevents baffling import failures.
terms: require/module.exports — Node ka original module system.
Module by resolved filename; doosri baar cached.
lessons.what:
CommonJS code ko ek wrapper function mein band deta hai: (function(exports, require, module, __filename, __dirname){ ... }). Isliye aap ke variables file-scoped (module-scoped) hote hain, global nahi.

require() 4 steps: resolve (path/extension) → load (read) → compile (wrapper + run) → cache (by filename). Doosri baar require = cached, dobara run nahi.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant recipe file: jab koi dish (module) maange, chef (require) recipe dhoondta (resolve), padhta (load), banata (compile), aur cost plate ke paas yaad rakhta (cache) taaki dobara cooking na karni pade.
lessons.why: Ye saare module confusion ka root hai — why variables scoped, why cache matters (singleton), circular deps. Module system wahi pehli 1000 lines hota hai jo process chalu hote hi chal-te. Interview resolution algorithm yahi se.

lessons.q: How does ESM work in Node.js? What are the differences between ESM and CommonJS?
lessons.qsub: ESM is the future of Node.js — interoperability with CJS is the most common source of confusion.

lessons.what:
ESM (import/export) JS ka official spec module system. Node isko support karta via: .mjs extension ya package.json mein "type":"module". CommonJS files ko .cjs ya default (type commonjs) se.

Interop: CJS require karke ESM ko default import se le sakta (as a CJS-style export), par named exports kabhi kabhi tricky. Static analysis (import is hoisted, async) ESM ko bundlers se alag banata — tree-shaking possible.
lessons.analogy: Standard kitchen rack (ESM) — har item ki jagah likhi hoti (static import, hoisted) to soff (bundler) sab pehche se samajh kar optimize kar sakta (tree-shake). Purana langot system (CJS) item tab dakhta hai jab bulao (dynamic require) — pehle se nahi dekh sakta.
lessons.why: ESM ab future hai — static, spec, tree-shakable. CJS node ka legacy. Interop (mix in ek project) sabse aam confusion. Interview "ESM vs CJS" crisp diff = senior signal.

lessons.name: Module caching, circular dependency handling
lessons.desc: Node caches modules by resolved filename. Circular deps return partially-built exports (module.exports is returned even if incomplete).
lessons.q: How does Node.js cache modules and handle circular dependencies?
lessons.qsub: Circular dependency edge cases show up in large codebases — understanding partial exports is critical.
terms: require by resolved path → same object.
A require B, B require A.
Cache = module ek baar run, sab same instance.
lessons.what:
Node modules ko resolved filename se cache karta hai. Isliye require('./a') do baar → same object (singleton), code ek baar hi chala.

Circular dependency (A→B→A): jab B A ko require karta hai, A abhi incomplete ho sakta — Node partially-built module.exports return karta hai (jo ab tak set hua). Matlab circular mein aapko wo property nahi milegi jo B ke require ke baad A mein add hui.
lessons.analogy: Do dost kaam share kar rahe (A aur B). B A se "dairy le aa" maangta hai jab A abhi adha kaam kar raha hai — A wahi de deta jo ab tak bana hai (partial). Poora banana ho to call me function (lazy), jo baad mein resolve ho.
lessons.why: Circular deps bade codebase mein hoti hai — partial exports se silent undefined bug. Isko jaana = common senior interview. Cache ka matlab bhi singleton — state sharing.

lessons.name: child_process: spawn, exec, fork, execFile, IPC
lessons.desc: child_process creates OS processes. spawn() streams I/O, exec() buffers, fork() spawns Node with IPC channel.
lessons.q: What is the difference between spawn, exec, fork, and execFile in child_process?
lessons.qsub: Multiprocess architecture is how production Node scales — each approach has different memory/speed tradeoffs.
terms: Streams stdio — ipc/commands, no buffering by default.
Direct binary, no shell — safe with args.
spawn + IPC channel — naya Node child.
lessons.what:
child_process ne OS-level processes. 4 tarike:

spawn() — streams I/O, large output sahi (bash/scripts). exec() — small shell command, buffers output (size limit!). execFile() — direct executable bina shell (injection save). fork() — Node child + IPC channel (message passing).

Choose kaise: shebang/pipe chahiye? spawn. Chhota buffer + shell? exec. Binary bina shell? execFile. Node worker + messages? fork.
lessons.analogy: Manager hiring: spawn = contractor ko direct kaam do (streams output). exec = "kaam karke poora result laana" (buffer). execFile = sirf direct tool, koi shell interpreter nahi. fork = apna hi team member (Node child) jo walkie-talkie (IPC) se baat kare.
lessons.why: Multiprocess scaling production ka base — each has memory/speed tradeoff. spawn vs exec ka classic: output size + shell injection. Fork = IPC da real state. Interview 4-way diff crisp = strong signal.

lessons.name: cluster module: load balancing, sticky sessions, restart strategies
lessons.desc: cluster forks worker processes sharing server ports. Master process distributes connections via round-robin (default).
lessons.q: How does the cluster module enable multi-core scaling in Node.js?
lessons.qsub: Cluster is Node's built-in horizontal scaling — understanding it is essential for production multi-core deployments.
terms: Master forks workers sharing server ports.
Worker crash par master naya spawn.
lessons.what:
cluster multi-core scaling Node ka built-in. Master process workers ko fork karta hai; sab workers ek hi server port share karte hain. Master connections ko slave workers mein round-robin distribute karta hai (default Linux).

Har worker apni event loop + memory — isliye N cores = N event loops. Sticky sessions zaroori jahan state/per-socket association (WebSocket) — same client same worker. Worker crash par master naya spawn (zero-downtime restart).
lessons.analogy: Hotel reception: ek telephone operator (master) jo calls (connections) ko N room-attendants (workers) mein round-robin banata hai. Har attendant apni line (event loop) sambhalta. Agar attendant kaam chhod de (crash), operator turant naya attendant hire karta (restart).
lessons.why: Node single core existential hota — cluster to use multi-core. Production scaling ka default. Interview "how Node uses all cores?" → cluster/PM2. Sticky session awareness = WebSocket deploy me zaroori.

lessons.name: worker_threads: shared memory, MessageChannel, use cases
lessons.desc: Worker threads run JS in parallel with their own V8 instance. Communication via message passing or SharedArrayBuffer.
lessons.q: When should you use worker_threads instead of child_process or cluster?
lessons.qsub: Worker threads are the only way to do CPU-bound work in Node without blocking the event loop.
terms: JS threads in same process, parallel execution.
Ye bina event loop block kaam karte.
lessons.what:
worker_threads JS ko parallel chalata hai — har worker ka apna V8 instance + event loop, same process (no OS process spawn like child_process). Ye CPU-bound kaam ke liye — event loop block na karne ko.

Communication: message passing (postMessage, structured clone) ya SharedArrayBuffer (shared raw memory, atomics). Use case: image processing, hashing, parsing, compression — compute-heavy libraries. VS child_process (heavier, OS process). VS cluster (multi-instance).
lessons.analogy: Factory with floors: child_process = alag-alag buildings (heavy, own kitchen). worker_threads = ek hi building ke alag floors — machine (CPU) shared, har floor apna supervisor (event loop). Compute-heavy kaam (maths/rendering) sub-floor ko bhejo taaki main floor khali reh (event loop responsive).
lessons.why: Node async I/O leta hai, par CPU work event loop rukata. worker_threads — only way CPU work bina block. Interview "CPU-bound in Node?" ka answer. Isolates which opts heavy.

lessons.name: Process lifecycle: signals, exit codes, graceful shutdown
lessons.desc: Node process lifecycle goes: initialization → event loop → exit. SIGTERM/SIGINT for clean shutdown, uncaughtException for crashes.
lessons.q: How do you implement a graceful shutdown in a Node.js application?
lessons.qsub: Graceful shutdown is what separates production-grade services from prototypes — it's a top-tier interview topic.
terms: Catch-all crash — log then exit (not re-run loop).
lessons.what:
Node process lifecycle: init → event loop → exit. SIGTERM/SIGINT se graceful shutdown implement hota — server close, DB disconnect, in-flight requests drain, phir exit 0.

SIGKILL ko catch nahi kar sakte (force). uncaughtException: handle to karo, par process ko maro (state unsafe) — restart supervisor (PM2) se. Exit codes: 0 ok, non-zero error.
lessons.analogy: Office bandh: SIGTERM = manager bolta "office bandh kar do properly" — files save (DB disconnect), client kaam finish (drain), lights band (exit 0). SIGINT = same. SIGKILL = bidi booting fire — band ho gaya bina save. uncaughtException = koi desk par virus paida ho gaya (corrupt) — building ko khulke do (exit), janitor (PM2) aage laayega.
lessons.why: Production-grade service = graceful shutdown. Bina ye, deploys mein requests drop, data loss. Top-tier interview topic. Ye hi apne service ko "production-grade" banata hai.

lessons.name: Stream types: Readable, Writable, Transform, Duplex
lessons.desc: Streams are EventEmitter instances with specific internal states. Readable reads data, Writable writes, Duplex does both, Transform modifies.
lessons.q: What are the four types of streams in Node.js and when do you use each?
lessons.qsub: Streams are Node's primary data abstraction — every HTTP request, file read, and pipe uses them internally.
terms: Source of data — file, HTTP request body. Aap khud data chunte ho.
Data ka destination — file, HTTP response. Aap data bhejte ho.
Readable + Writable dono — net socket, zlib.
Duplex jo data modify karta hai — compress/encrypt (gzip).
lessons.what:
Streams Node ka data abstraction hai — har I/O toota-tuta data behta hai chunks mein, poora ek saath memory mein nahi. 4 types: Readable (data deta hai), Writable (leti hai), Duplex (dono), Transform (Duplex jo modification karta hai) chunki "pass-through" jo bhaant data.

Har stream internally EventEmitter hai apne khud ke states ke saath. Http request/response, file read, pipe — sab stream hi hain.
lessons.analogy: Nahi paani ki pipeline: Readable = tanki (paani/data source), Writable = geti (destination), Duplex = dono taraf open pipe, Transform = filter (gandagi clean). Paani poora ek saath nahi aata, chunk-chunk (boond) behta hai.
lessons.why: Badi files/network sab memory-chunked hota hai. Poora buffer ek saath = OOM. Streams memory-boundary par kaam karte hain. Interview ka base — "every I/O is a stream".

lessons.name: Backpressure and highWaterMark internals
lessons.desc: Backpressure prevents overwhelming consumers. highWaterMark sets the buffer limit before pushback signals are sent.
lessons.q: What is backpressure in Node.js streams and how does highWaterMark control it?
lessons.qsub: Backpressure is the most common stream failure point — missing it causes OOM in production pipelines.
terms: Jab consumer sa slow hai, upstream incoming data tham deta hai.
Buffer size limit (default 16KB / 64KB) — iske baad pushback.
Readable internal buffer mein data daalta hai.
Writable async write method — callback = space free.
lessons.what:
Backpressure = data producer se kehna "aarām, main saath nahi de paa raha". Jab Writable ka internal buffer highWaterMark (default 16384 bytes) cross karta hai, return value false ho jati hai — aapko write() rokna hai jab tak drain event na aaye.

pipe()/pipeline() ye automatically handle karte hain. Memory-flooding prevent hoti hai, OOM nahi aata.
lessons.analogy: Bhoj aur waiter: kitchen (producer) se khana (data) chal raha hai par dining table (buffer) bhara hai. Waiter (pipe) kitchen ko signal deta hai "ruk, space bana" — jab table khali (drain event), phir aage. Agar ye na hota, table aur kitchen dono musibat.
lessons.why: Backpressure missing = unbounded memory growth → OOM crash. It's the "most common stream failure". production pipeline strings mein isi se bachte hain.

lessons.name: Buffer internals: alloc, pool, encoding, slice
lessons.desc: Buffer is a fixed-size chunk of raw memory allocated outside V8 heap. Uses internal pool for small allocations.
lessons.q: What is a Buffer in Node.js? What is the difference between Buffer.alloc and Buffer.allocUnsafe?
lessons.qsub: Buffer is the bridge between JS and binary data — nearly every I/O operation touches it.
terms: Fixed-size raw memory chunk, V8 heap ke bahar (native).
Fast — may leak old data, must overwrite.
8KB internal pool for small (<4KB) buffers — reuse.
lessons.what:
Buffer = JavaScript ka Uint8Array binary data handle — fixed-size, V8 heap ke bahar allocated native memory. Buffer.alloc(size) zero-fills (safe), Buffer.allocUnsafe(size) reuse (fast par uninitialized — old data dikh sakta hai). Chhote (<4KB) buffers ek shared 8KB pool se aate hain.

Encoding (utf8/base64/hex) aur slice (sparse view, no copy) bhi important.
lessons.analogy: Chalk-board vs fresh chalk: alloc = naye peely chalk-board (safe, empty). allocUnsafe = pehle istemal kiya board — fast dikhaya, par us par purani writing reh sakti hai (unsafe). Pool = sharda chalk sticks ek dabbe se.
lessons.why: I/O (file/network) binary data deta hai — JS strings don't cut it. Buffer bridges JS ↔ raw bytes. Interview "binary data" ka yahi base hai.

lessons.name: pipeline() vs pipe() — error handling and cleanup
lessons.desc: pipe() chains readable → writable but doesn't forward errors. pipeline() auto-destroys all streams on any error.
lessons.q: Why is stream.pipeline() preferred over pipe() in production Node.js code?
lessons.qsub: Using pipe() without proper error handling is the #1 Node.js production bug — always prefer pipeline().
terms: Chains read→write, no error forwarding, no auto-destroy.
Auto-destroys all streams on error; handles backpressure.
pipeline takes final cb for completion/error.
lessons.what:
source.pipe(dest) simple chaining deta hai, par error forward nahi karta aur fail hone par streams destroy nahi hoti — leaks/hanging. stream.pipeline(src, ...dests, cb) sab handle karta hai: koi error aaye par saari streams destroy ho jati hain, backpressure bhi manage hota hai.

Production mein hamesha pipeline() prefer karo.
lessons.analogy: Agnishamak bucket chain: pipe = bas haath se haath bucket (agar beech mein koi gir jaye, koi nahi jaanta — aag aur bucket rukti hai). pipeline = supervisor jo dekhta hai ki sab participate karein, koi gire (error) par turant full chain rok de aur saaf kare (destroy).
lessons.why: pipe() bina error handling = #1 Node production bug (leaked handles, hanging pipelines). interview "why pipeline over pipe" ka core.

lessons.name: Custom streams implementation (Readable/Writable/Transform)
lessons.desc: Extend stream.Readable etc. and implement _read/_write/_transform. Use for data format parsers, protocol encoders, etc.
lessons.q: How do you implement a custom Readable or Transform stream in Node.js?
lessons.qsub: Custom streams are how production libraries handle non-trivial I/O — used in databases, queues, and parsers.
terms: Readable implement — dekh ke push() data.
Transform implement — cb(null, out) with modified data.
Readable buffer mein data daalta hai.
lessons.what:
Custom stream banane ke liye stream.Readable/Writable/Transform ko extend karo aur underscore methods implement karo. Readable: _read() mein push() karke data bajao, push(null) = end. Writable: _write(chunk, enc, cb) — cb() bulao jab processed. Transform: _transform(chunk, enc, cb) — cb(null, result).

Yahi tarike se parsers, protocol encoders, DB drivers banate hain.
lessons.analogy: Factory assembly line: Aap machine (custom stream) ke rules set karte ho. Readable machine = apna maal utpann karta hai (push). Writable = maal le kar kaam karta hai (cb). Transform = maal ko badal kar aage bhejta hai (cb with result). Har machine apna math token saap hota hai.
lessons.why: Production libraries (DB, queues, parsers) bina custom stream nahi bante. Interview "how to build a stream" ka practical answer.

lessons.qsub: Text streams with multi-byte characters produce corrupted output without proper decoder handling.

lessons.what:
string_decoder.StringDecoder ek text stream par multi-byte characters (emoji, 中, accented) ke partial/cut-off chunks ko sahi se jodta hai. Agar char do chunks mein toota hai, StringDecoder use buffer karta hai taaki write() par garbled na nikle.

lessons.name: V8 compilation pipeline: Ignition, TurboFan, Sparkplug
lessons.desc: V8 uses a multi-tier compiler: Ignition (fast bytecode interpreter) → Sparkplug (quick baseline compiler) → TurboFan (optimizing JIT).
lessons.q: How does V8 compile JavaScript? Walk me through the Ignition, Sparkplug, and TurboFan pipeline.
lessons.qsub: Understanding V8's compilation tiers explains why some code runs 100x faster — and when deoptimization kills perf.
terms: Fast interpreter — code ko bytecode banata hai.
Quick baseline compiler — bytecode → machine code.
Optimizing JIT — hot code ko highly optimized code.
Optimized code invalid ho jaye to wapas interpreter.
lessons.what:
V8 code ko multi-tier compile karta hai: 1) Ignition — JS ko bytecode interpret karta hai (fast start). 2) Sparkplug — bytecode ka quick baseline machine code (start + speed balance). 3) TurboFan — frequently-run (hot) code ko aggressively optimize karta hai, 100x faster.

Deoptimization = assumptions (monomorphic types) fail honey par optimized code gir jata hai — slow. Isliye type stability zaroori.
lessons.analogy: Cooking shows: Ignition = pehle-dil khaane se turant recipe samajha (fast start). Sparkplug = aadha tez paka liya. TurboFan = jo dish baar-baar banti, uske liye khud ka special kitchen banaya — 100x tez. Agar ingredients (types) badal gaye to special kitchen bekaar (deopt) aur basic kitchen par wapis.
lessons.why: Ye hi batata hai ki kyun kuch code 100x fast hota hai — aur kyu type flipping se perf girti hai. Top V8 perf topic.

lessons.name: Hidden classes, inline caching, and Shapes
lessons.desc: V8 represents object shapes (hidden classes) to track property offsets. Inline caching (IC) accelerates property access by caching shape lookups.
lessons.q: What are hidden classes in V8 and how do they affect JavaScript performance?
lessons.qsub: Hidden classes are why monomorphic code in tight loops is 100x faster than polymorphic — a top perf interview topic.
terms: Property access ka shape lookup cache — fast path.
lessons.what:
V8 har object par ek hidden class / Shape track karta hai jo property ke offsets ko yaad rakhta hai. Property access par Inline Caching use hota hai: agar shape same hamesha, lookup cache ho jata hai — monomorphic = fastest. Agar object ki shape alag-alag hoti hai (polymorphic), cache miss — slow.

Isliye consistent object shape (same key order, no adding properties later) perf ke liye critical hai.
lessons.analogy: Library bookshelf cards: Hidden class = har booko ka same "location card" (shelf-offset). Agar saari books ek jaisi shape (same layout), librarian (IC) ko exact shelf yaad hai — instant (monomorphic). Agar har book alag jagh aata hai, har baar dhundna pade (polymorphic cache miss) — slow.
lessons.why: Monomorphic code in tight loops = 100x faster than polymorphic. Perf interview ka hidden-gem — "why object shape matters".

lessons.name: Memory management: Orinoco GC, young/old gen, V8 heap
lessons.desc: V8 heap has young generation (semi-space, scavenge), old generation (mark-sweep-compact), and large object space. Orinoco is the concurrent GC.
lessons.q: How does V8's garbage collector work? What are the young and old generations?
lessons.qsub: GC pauses are the #1 Node.js latency source — understanding GC phases is critical for production Node tuning.
terms: Naya data — semi-space, scavenge copy GC.
lessons.what:
V8 heap generations mein banta hai. Young gen (semi-space ×2): naye objects, cheap scavenge (copy survivor). Old gen: survivors mark-sweep-compact (dead mark + free + compact). Orinoco = concurrent/parallel GC jo main thread ko minor rokta hai.

GC pause latency ka #1 source hai production Node mein.
lessons.analogy: Office desk: Young gen = in-tray (naye papers). Scavenge = chhoti saaf-safai, jaldi papers trash ya "keep" box. Keep box (old gen) = important files, kabhi-kabhi bade cleanup (mark-sweep) — desk organize. Orinoco = cleaning staff jo aapka kaam rokke bina background mein saaf karta hai.
lessons.why: GC = main latency source. Ye jaana = production Node tuning, heap dumps, leak diagnosis ka base.

lessons.name: Memory leaks: detection, heap snapshots, Chrome DevTools
lessons.desc: Memory leaks appear as monotonically growing heap. Common causes: global references, closures, timers, detached DOM-like patterns.
lessons.q: How do you detect and fix memory leaks in a Node.js application?
lessons.qsub: Memory leaks cause crashes and degraded performance — detecting them is an essential production skill.
terms: Callback badi scope ko hold kare.
Gone from DOM but still referenced.
lessons.what:
Memory leak = heap monotonically growing — objects release nahi hote. Common causes: 1) global references (unintended global.x), 2) closures (callback big parent scope hold kare), 3) timers/listeners not cleaned, 4) caches bina eviction.

Detection: --inspect → Chrome DevTools → heap snapshot compare; use --max-old-space-size + monitoring.
lessons.analogy: Chhota bhandaar: Kapde (objects) har din aate hain par koi nahi bahar nikalta — godam bharta hi jata hai (heap grows). Root cause: koi "purana list" (global/closure) har cheez pakre rakha hai. Heap snapshot = godam ka poora inventory, jaise kapdo ka silsila jahan phas gaya dikhta hai.
lessons.why: Leaks = crash + degraded perf. Production skill — har serious Node app is detection ko janta hai.

lessons.name: Error types: operational vs programmer errors
lessons.desc: Operational errors (ECONNREFUSED, timeout) are runtime problems. Programmer errors (TypeError, ReferenceError) are bugs that should crash.
lessons.q: What is the difference between operational errors and programmer errors in Node.js?

Operational errors = runtime mishaps (network, user input) — inhe handle karo, retry/graceful degrade. Programmer errors = actual bugs (TypeError) — state corrupt, inhe crash + restart (PM2) karo, loop mein chhu nahi.

Ye classification hi robust error handling ka foundation hai.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant: Operational = khana khatam ho gaya / sagee aaya nahi (aap filter/double-check karte ho — retry). Programmer = chef recipe galat likh kar seelha de diya (bug) — isse aage kaam karwana jaalim hai, kitchen ko rok ke fix karo. Dono ko same tareeke se nahi treat karna.

lessons.name: Async error propagation: try/catch, Promise rejections, callback errors
lessons.desc: Async errors don't propagate via try/catch automatically. Promises use .catch(), callbacks use err-first pattern.
lessons.q: How do errors propagate in async Node.js code? What catches unhandled Promise rejections?
lessons.qsub: Unhandled async errors cause silent failures — understanding propagation prevents haunted production bugs.
terms: Sync errors only — async mein kaam nahi.
lessons.what: Async errors try/catch se auto-propogate nahi hota — kyunki await/callback kaam alag task par. Patterns: async/await + try/catch (clean), .catch(), ya err-first callback cb(err, data). unhandledRejection event bina .catch() ke reject hone par fire hota hai — global safety net, par hamesha explicit catch prefer.
lessons.analogy: Package delivery: try/catch = aap apne ghar (sync) ke andar galti pakadte ho. Promise/await = courier (async task) — aapne await kiya; agar courier galti kare, error catch (return slip) se milta hai. err-first = courier "yahan error chhod gaya" bata deta hai. unhandledRejection = aisaa package jo kisi ko nahi mila — post office alert.
lessons.why: Unhandled async errors = silent failures / haunted prod bugs. Propagation samajhna = non-negotiable.

lessons.name: Dockerizing Node.js: multi-stage builds, signals, health checks
lessons.desc: Node Docker images should be optimized with multi-stage builds, proper signal handling, and health check endpoints.
lessons.q: How do you properly Dockerize a Node.js application with production best practices?
lessons.qsub: Containerized Node is today's default deployment — mistakes here cause crashes, bloat, and slow restarts.
lessons.what: Good Node Dockerfile: multi-stage (node:alpine build deps → distroless/runtime with only deps), non-root user, SIGTERM gracefully handle (kill npm/foreman → exec form), /health endpoint, dependency caching via layer order. Use EXPOSE, npm ci --omit=dev.

lessons.name: Rate limiting, circuit breakers, and resilience patterns
lessons.desc: Rate limiting prevents abuse. Circuit breakers stop cascading failures. Both are essential for production API services.
lessons.q: How would you implement rate limiting and circuit breakers in a Node.js API?
lessons.qsub: Resilience patterns are what make services survive production traffic — they're core to system design interviews.

lessons.what: Rate limiting (express-rate-limit/token bucket) per-IP abuse control → 429. Circuit breaker: jab external call fail hone lage threshold par, circuit open — direct fallback/cache, dependency recover hone par half-open test → close. Prevents cascading failures.

lessons.name: GraphQL with Node: Apollo Server, resolvers, DataLoader
lessons.desc: Apollo Server handles GraphQL execution. DataLoader batches and caches database requests per request cycle.
lessons.q: How does DataLoader solve the N+1 query problem in a GraphQL Node.js server?
lessons.qsub: GraphQL is the modern API paradigm — DataLoader solves the N+1 problem that makes naive GraphQL slow.
terms: Batches + caches DB calls per request cycle.
Per parent item 1 extra query — explosion.
lessons.what: GraphQL queries N parent items (e.g. 10 books), har parent ka resolver field apni DB query run karta hai → N+1 (11 queries). DataLoader same batch ke andar queries ko group karta hai (inId order) aur per-request cache — sirf 1-2 queries. Apollo Server resolvers isi se hook karte hain.
lessons.analogy: Library lookup: N+1 = har book (parent) ke liye alag counter par jaao (per-author query) — 10 books = 10 extra runs. DataLoader = ek baar saare authors ki list le kar ek registry banao (batch via inId) aur is request mein peeche se (cache) — sirf 1 trip.
lessons.why: Naive GraphQL = N+1 explosion → slow. DataLoader = standard fix; core modern-API knowledge.

lessons.name: crypto module — hashing, HMAC, encryption, randomBytes, pbkdf2
lessons.desc: crypto.createHash for SHA-256/MD5 hashing. crypto.createHmac for HMAC. crypto.scrypt/pbkdf2 for password hashing. crypto.randomBytes for secure random. crypto.createCipheriv for AES encryption. Never use crypto.createCipher (deprecated).

lessons.what: crypto: createHash SHA-256 (integrity, not passwords). createHmac hash+key (signing). Passwords → scrypt/pbkdf2 (deliberately slow). randomBytes secure tokens/salts. createCipheriv AES with IV encryption. Never createCipher (deprecated/unsecure).
lessons.analogy: Stamp vs signature vs safe: hash = fingerprint — kisi bhi document ka patta (integrity), koi secret nahi. lessons.why: Security basics har backend mein. Password hashing approach = security question staple; wrong = leak risk.

lessons.name: net module — TCP server/client, sockets, pipe
lessons.desc: net.createServer for TCP servers. net.createConnection for TCP clients. Socket is a duplex stream. socket.pipe() for backpressure-safe data transfer. Foundation for HTTP servers and custom protocols.
lessons.q: How do you create a basic TCP server in Node.js? What is the relationship between net and http modules?
lessons.qsub: What is backpressure in Node.js streams? How does pipe() handle it?
lessons.what: net = raw TCP layer. net.createServer TCP server; connection par ek Socket (duplex stream). net.createConnection client. socket.pipe() backpressure-safe transfer. Ye foundation hai — http module itself net par built hai; custom protocols bhi yahin se bante hain.
lessons.analogy: Landline vs operator: net = raw phone line (TCP) — data ka channel, bas bits. http = operator (protocol) jo "hello/hi, GET /" rules add karta hai. Socket = ready two-way phone call — dono baat kar sakte (duplex). socket.pipe = transfer session bina rukawat where aage piche sync.
lessons.why: TCP = transport foundation; http/https sab isi par. Custom protocols (in-house wire) net se. Core-layer understanding.

lessons.name: TLS/SSL — createServer with TLS, certificates, SNI, HTTPS
lessons.desc: tls.createServer wraps net.createServer with TLS. Requires certificate and key. SNI (Server Name Indication) enables multiple domains on one IP. https module is HTTP over TLS. Let's Encrypt for free certificates.
lessons.q: How do you set up HTTPS in Node.js? What is SNI and why is it important?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between tls and https modules? How does certificate validation work?
terms: Server Name Indication — multiple domains one IP.
lessons.what: tls.createServer({ cert, key }) net server par TLS layer add. SNI allows ek IP par multiple domains — handshake mein hostname ke hisab se cert choice. https module = HTTP over TLS. Certs Let's Encrypt (free ACME). Validation = chain (leaf→intermediate→root CA) trust.
lessons.analogy: Locked letter + postmark: TLS = sealed, encrypted letters (no snooping). cert+key = post office ke official seal proving kiska letter (identity). SNI = ek hi phys address par multiple tenements (domains) — batao kis naam ka dabba (cert choose by hostname). Let's Encrypt = free seal issuing post office. Chain = package seal → postman → head office trust chain.
lessons.why: HTTPS = mandatory today. SNI, cert validation, self-signed — every Node deployment touches.

lessons.name: npm workspaces — monorepo management, hoisting, shared dependencies
lessons.desc: npm workspaces manage multiple packages in one repo. Root package.json has 'workspaces' field. Dependencies hoist to root node_modules. Use npm run --workspace for scoped scripts. Alternatives: pnpm workspaces, yarn workspaces, turborepo.
lessons.q: How do npm workspaces work? What is dependency hoisting and what problems does it cause?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between npm workspaces and yarn workspaces? When would you use turborepo with workspaces?
terms: Shared deps ek root node_modules mein — no dup.
npm run in a specific package.
lessons.what: npm workspaces: ek monorepo mein multiple packages (packages/*). Root package.json mein "workspaces": ["packages/*"]. Dependencies hoist hoti hain shared root node_modules (no duplication). npm run --workspace=a scoped. pnpm/yarn alternatives — pnpm strict (no phantom deps). turborepo adds cached task runner on top.
lessons.analogy: Apartment building: workspaces = ek building (repo) mein multiple flats (packages). Hoisting = shared plumbing/electricity (common deps) building ke basement — har flat alag nahi lagata (no duplication). --workspace = flat-specific maintenance. pnpm = strict kya aap apne flat se dusre flat ka maal use kar sakte — nahi (phantom dep prevent). Turborepo = building manager jo saare flats ka renovation cache karta hai.
lessons.why: Monorepo management = modern large-team standard; shared code, atomic changes, one CI. Interview-relevant.
